problem_statement: When an IPv6 interface that disables Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) goes DOWN and comes back UP, its multicast-group join state is lost. A joined multicast address should remain marked as joined across an interface down/up transition on such an interface (e.g. OpenThread), so that multicast packets continue to be accepted; but currently the join state is cleared on interface down and is not restored on interface up. Conversely, on an interface where MLD is enabled, the join state should be cleared on interface down and then correctly rejoined when the interface comes back up.

verification.reason: The core behavior is specified, but the exact flag name and observable reference/joined-state requirements are not fully stated, so they should be added without changing the implementation direction.

problems.detail: The hidden checks use the interface flag NET_IF_IPV6_NO_MLD, but the statement only refers to MLD being disabled without naming that flag.

The hidden checks expect the multicast address object reference count to remain 1 after add/join and across down/up transitions, and expect net_if_ipv6_maddr_is_joined to return true or false in specific cases; the statement does not state these exact observable values.
The hidden checks require that clearing the joined state does not remove the multicast address entry and that the entry remains removable later, which the statement does not make explicit.

problem_statement_fixed: When an IPv6 interface that disables Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD), as indicated by the NET_IF_IPV6_NO_MLD interface flag, goes DOWN and comes back UP, its multicast-group join state is lost. A joined multicast address should remain marked as joined both while the interface is down and after it is brought back up on such an interface (e.g. OpenThread), so that multicast packets continue to be accepted; but currently the join state is cleared on interface down and is not restored on interface up. Conversely, on an interface where MLD is enabled (NET_IF_IPV6_NO_MLD is not set), the join state should be cleared on interface down and then correctly rejoined when the interface comes back up. In both cases, the multicast address entry itself and its reference count must not change during the interface down/up transition; for a multicast address that has been added once and then joined, the reference count should remain 1 through the transition.
